subject: NovaBlue private cluster onboarding — scope & tech playcall notes
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@novablue.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@novablue.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment inquiry — NovaBlue: core requirements + quick intro

Hi Monica / Aditya,

Thanks for taking the time to sync. We're evaluating a private, on-prem deployment of Redwood for inference workloads behind our VPC. High level context: NovaBlue will host inference nodes in our colo racks (primary site) and have a DR site in a separate colo region. Primary concerns are network isolation, predictable low tail latency for model serving, and strict data residency + KMS controls.

Topline asks from our side:
- Desired latency target: P95 < 60ms for 2k concurrent sessions (model mix includes Llama2-70B quantized + an internal 13B)
- We will provide 12U of GPU servers at launch (expected to be A10G-equivalent / 4x A10 GPUs per server) and want Redwood to recommend node pool slices and storage layout
- Need KMS integration (HashiCorp Vault currently) and audit log export to our SIEM (Splunk)
- Network: we operate BGP across racks, closed egress, and will require explicit egress rules for telemetry only

Can we run a short playcall tomorrow to capture requirements and get an intake checklist from Redwood? I attached our rough rack inventory.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Infrastructure Lead — NovaBlue
[Attachment: novablue-rack-inventory.csv (text/csv)]

- Do you have a preferred CSI driver (Ceph, NetApp, local-ssd) or should we propose?
- Will there be an internal NTP/PKI and an existing Vault instance for KMS (sounds like yes) — who owns vault admin?

Attached: Redwood intake checklist (lightweight) and a first-pass nodepool sizing spreadsheet for us to discuss.

I'll also loop Karthik for network specifics.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.k@novablue.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 13:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — NovaBlue: core requirements + quick intro

Samira / team — adding a few technical notes ahead of the call so we can validate assumptions quickly:

Node pool and storage quick proposal (first-pass):
- Control plane: 3x m6i-like dedicated control-plane VMs (or equivalent baremetal management nodes). Control plane should be on a management VLAN with no tenant workloads.
- Compute node pools: 
  - model-serving-pool (GPU): expected 12x GPU servers -> recommend 2 node classes: 
    * gpu-large: 6 servers (4x A10 each), tainted gpu=true:NoSchedule, each server should run a kubelet with device plugin for MIG or GPU passthrough as applicable
    * gpu-small: 6 servers (4x A10 each) reserved for smaller models/parallel sessions, configured with smaller pod limits and lower eviction priority
  - inference-frontend: 3x CPU nodes for routing, load balancing, shims (HPA not recommended for GPU pods)
- Storage:
  - model-cache: local NVMe per server for KV / model shard cache (fast path), backed up periodically to a shared object store for warm-starts
  - persistent-volumes: recommend Ceph/Rook or NetApp CSI if you want shared RWX volumes for batching and checkpoints; otherwise use ReadWriteOnce blockstore for model weights
  - logs/metrics: dedicated NFS or networked block store with retention policy and lifecycle to object storage (S3-compatible)
- Networking:
  - Pod CIDR: 10.244.0.0/16 (tunable)
  - Service CIDR: 10.96.0.0/12
  - MetalLB for baremetal LB or use your existing edge LB via BGP peering; we prefer MetalLB configured in layer2 mode if BGP peering is not available
  - Egress: restrict outbound to Redwood telemetry endpoints + your SIEM collector; allow KMS endpoints to Vault host(s)
- Security:
  - KMS: integrate with Vault transit for envelope encryption; require access from control-plane only for signing tokens
  - Audit: enable AuditSink to forward to Splunk via Fluentd; retention per your compliance needs

I'll bring a sizing workbook to the call (attached) with expected per-GPU throughput estimates for Llama2-70B quantized and a 13B baseline.

— Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
[Attachment: nodepool-sizing-proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@novablue.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — NovaBlue: core requirements + quick intro

Thanks for the pre-read — a few clarifications from our infra team after reviewing your notes: 

1) GPUs: the units are Ampere A10G-equivalent (we'll confirm exact firmware), but we plan to carve MIG profiles in production. Is Redwood compatible with mixed MIG/no-MIG nodes?
2) Storage: we prefer local NVMe for model cache, but need a recommended retention policy for model shards — 48 hours cold cache + weekly snapshot to object store?
3) Networking: we will do BGP peering from our TORs; we need guidance on firewall rules for egress to your telemetry and for Vault calls (Vault is on a management VLAN at 10.10.254.0/24).

Also attaching a quick network CIDR diagram and our current vault admin contact. Can you update the intake checklist with exact firewall ports and IAM roles required by Redwood?

Regards,
Daniel Ortiz
Sr. SRE — NovaBlue
[Attachment: network-cidr-diagram.png (image/png)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@novablue.com>, Daniel Ortiz <d.ortiz@novablue.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment inquiry — NovaBlue: core requirements + quick intro

Daniel / Samira — thanks, this is helpful. Action items from Redwood: 

- We'll validate MIG compatibility: short answer — yes, Redwood runtime supports mixed MIG/no-MIG nodes; we recommend grouping similar MIG profiles into separate node classes for scheduling efficiency. (Aditya will share a short compatibility matrix.)
- Model-cache retention: we propose 48h warm cache + asynchronous snapshot to S3 weekly; we'll include a toggle in the deployment manifest to adjust retention windows.
- Firewall & ports: attached to this thread is a precise ports matrix and minimal IAM roles (we only need service account credentials for the control-plane agents; tokens rotated by Vault).
- Next steps: schedule a technical deep-dive Thurs 09:00 PST to walk rack wiring, BGP peering, and Vault integration. I'll send calendar invites after this mail.

Attached: ports-and-iam-matrix.csv, redwood-deploy-operator-roles.md

If you can confirm the Vault admin contact and a timeline for node firmware confirmation, we can lock in the preflight checklist and deliver the final nodepool sizing by Fri.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ports-and-iam-matrix.csv (text/csv)]
